EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows two distinct strong peaks in the triple-bond region: 2251 cm⁻¹ (typical for a C≡N stretch, Nakamoto rule GFQ-009) and a second band at 2340 cm⁻¹ that matches a P–H stretching vibration (GFQ-007, SUB-008). Among the candidates only molecule 8 ([C-]# [N+]c1nc[pH]c1Br) contains both a nitrile group and a P–H bond, naturally giving rise to these two separate bands. The bands at 703 cm⁻¹ and 788 cm⁻¹ correspond well to aromatic C–H out-of-plane deformations (expected 650-900 cm⁻¹) and can also include C–Br stretches, consistent with the brominated heteroaromatic ring in 8. The mid-frequency ring modes at 1272 and 1433 cm⁻¹ and the C–H stretches at 2962/3005 cm⁻¹ are likewise appropriate for an aromatic molecule bearing alkyl hydrogen atoms. No other candidate simultaneously provides a nitrile and a P–H bond to account for the key 2251 cm⁻¹ and 2340 cm⁻¹ peaks, making candidate 8 the best fit.
